description:
Simulate a Rust circuit: power on every wire and which devices run. The circuit simulator's solver (https://rust.wiki/calculators/circuit-simulator), Rust's power rules since the
April 2024 rework: each part's `inputs` and `outputs` (rW), whether it's `on`, device and battery `status`
("Needs 10, gets 4", "Empty in 4 h 0 min"), the power on every wire, `power_generated`, `devices_on` of
`devices_total`, and a `page` link that opens the same circuit on the board. A device takes its full draw or
nothing; splitters share evenly between connected outputs; batteries give only what the parts after them draw,
up to their maximum. Wiring something back into itself is reported as `short_circuit`. Part and device names come from get_circuit_parts / get_electricity_data. Give the user the page link: it opens the circuit on the interactive board.

parts.description: Comma-separated `label:Part` - a part from /calculators/circuit-simulator (Large Solar Panel, Wind Turbine, Large Battery, Splitter, Electrical Branch, Switch, AND Switch...) or a powered device by name (Auto Turret, Ceiling Light, SAM Site...). Settings in brackets: `b:Large Battery(charge=50)`, `br:Electrical Branch(b=10)`, `sw:Switch(state=0)`.
examples: s:Large Solar Panel,b:Large Battery,t:Auto Turret,l:Ceiling Light

wires.description: Comma-separated `from>to` wires between labels, each end optionally `.port` - a port name or 1-based number (`sp.Out 2>t`, `br.Branch Out>l`, `g>sw.Switch On`). Default: first output to first input.

name: simulate_circuit
title: Simulate a Rust circuit: power on every wire and which devices run
